s: Who brought the libel suit that C. Sankaran Nair later lost?
x: Sankaran Nair lost Michael O'Dwyer's libel suit by an 11-1 verdict.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (Person)
A. Rabindranath Tagore
B. C. Sankaran Nair
C. Mahatma Gandhi
List-II (Protest)
1. Resigned from the Viceroy's Executive Council
2. Returned the Kaiser-i-Hind medal
3. Gave up his knighthood
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Tagore gave up his knighthood, Sankaran Nair resigned from the Viceroy's Executive Council and Gandhi returned the Kaiser-i-Hind medal.

s: On which date did Rabindranath Tagore renounce his knighthood?
x: Tagore returned his knighthood on 31 May 1919 in protest at the Jallianwala Bagh massacre.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the events of April 1919 in Punjab?
o: Kitchlew and Satyapal were arrested on 13 April 1919
The Jallianwala Bagh crowd had gathered for a protest and Baisakhi
A country-wide strike took place on 6 April 1919
The Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place on 13 April 1919
x: Dr. Saifuddin Kitchlew and Dr. Satyapal were arrested on 9 April 1919, not 13 April; 13 April was the day of the massacre.

s: On which date were Dr Saifuddin Kitchlew and Dr Satyapal arrested?
x: They were arrested on 9 April 1919, not 13 April, the day of the massacre.

s: Who ordered the firing at Jallianwala Bagh on 13 April 1919?
x: Brig.-Gen. Reginald Dyer ordered the firing; O'Dwyer was the Lt. Governor and Chelmsford the Viceroy.

s: Martial law in Amritsar and Lahore after 13 April 1919 included public floggings, aircraft strafing and which humiliating order?
x: Martial law included public floggings, aircraft strafing of protestors and the crawling order.

s: Who had been assaulted in the Amritsar lane to which the crawling order applied?
x: Indians had to crawl through the lane where the English missionary Marcella Sherwood had been assaulted.

s: Besides Amritsar, where was martial law imposed after 13 April 1919?
x: Martial law was imposed in Amritsar and Lahore under O'Dwyer's regime.

s: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre formed an important background to which movement?
x: By deepening hostility to British rule, the massacre prepared the ground for the Non-Cooperation Movement of 1920.

s: Which of the following was an outcome of the Jallianwala Bagh massacre?
x: After the massacre faith in British justice declined; the other events came before it.

s: During whose viceroyalty was the Rowlatt Act (Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act, 1919) repealed?
x: It was repealed under Lord Reading, along with the Press Act of 1910.

s: Under the Rowlatt Act, in-camera trials were held by a High Court panel of how many judges?
x: The Rowlatt Act provided in-camera trials by a three-judge High Court panel, with no right of appeal.

s: The Rowlatt Act came into existence as an extension of which Act?
x: The Rowlatt legislation extended the extraordinary powers earlier provided under the Defence of India Act, 1915.

s: Which Act was popularly described as 'No Vakil, No Appeal, No Daleel'?
x: The Rowlatt Act was called 'No Vakil, No Appeal, No Daleel' because it allowed detention without trial; Gandhi responded with the Rowlatt Satyagraha.

s:
Consider the following about protests against the Rowlatt Act:
1. Jinnah, Malaviya and Mazhar-ul-Haq drafted the Hunter Committee report.
2. Jinnah, Malaviya and Mazhar-ul-Haq resigned in opposition to the Act.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: Muhammad Ali Jinnah, Madan Mohan Malaviya and Mazhar-ul-Haq resigned in opposition to the Rowlatt legislation; they did not draft the Hunter Committee report.

s: In which year was the Sedition (Rowlatt) Committee, whose report led to the Rowlatt Act, appointed?
x: The Sedition Committee under Justice Sidney Rowlatt was appointed in 1917.

s: Who among the following resigned from the Imperial Legislative Council in protest against the Rowlatt Act?
x: Jinnah, Madan Mohan Malaviya and Mazhar-ul-Haq resigned from the Council against the Rowlatt Act; Sankaran Nair resigned from the Executive Council later.

s: Who headed the Sedition Committee of 1917, on whose report the Rowlatt Act was based?
x: The Sedition Committee (Rowlatt Committee), appointed in 1917, was headed by Justice Sidney Rowlatt.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Sedition Committee:
1. It was appointed in 1917.
2. It was headed by Lord William Hunter.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Sedition Committee of 1917 was headed by Justice Sidney Rowlatt; Lord Hunter headed the 1919 inquiry into the Punjab disorders.

s: On which date was the Rowlatt Act passed?
x: The Rowlatt Act was passed on 10 March 1919. 6 April was the date of the Rowlatt Satyagraha hartal, while 13 April was the date of the Jallianwala Bagh massacre.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: The Simon Commission arrived in 1928. The events of 1942 were the Cripps Mission and the Quit India Movement.

s: Which of the following events took place in 1920?
x: Tilak died on 1 August 1920; the Lucknow Pact was 1916, the Moplah Revolt 1921 and the Simon Commission 1928.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Champaran (1917) was the indigo satyagraha; Kheda (1918) was the peasant satyagraha, Ahmedabad (1918) the mill workers' strike and Dandi (1930) the Salt March.

s: Which movement did Gandhi withdraw after the Chauri Chaura violence of February 1922?
x: The Chauri Chaura violence of February 1922 made Gandhi withdraw the Non-Cooperation Movement.

s: In which year did the Dandi March take place?
x: The Dandi March was in 1930, after the Swadeshi Movement (1905) and Jallianwala Bagh (1919) and before Quit India (1942).

s: In which year was the Poona Pact signed?
x: The Poona Pact came in September 1932, after the Dandi March (1930) and the Gandhi–Irwin Pact (1931), and before Quit India (1942).

s:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
1. Chauri Chaura incident
2. Partition of Bengal
3. Gandhi-Irwin Pact
4. Simon Commission
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Partition of Bengal was in 1905, Chauri Chaura in 1922, the Simon Commission in 1928 and the Gandhi-Irwin Pact in 1931.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (Place / Movement)
A. Bardoli
B. Tebhaga
C. Pochampalli
D. Chauri Chaura
List-II (Associated with)
1. Bhoodan
2. Withdrawal of the Non-Cooperation Movement
3. Vallabhbhai Patel
4. Bengal
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Bardoli - Patel; Tebhaga - Bengal (Kisan Sabha); Pochampalli - Bhoodan (Vinoba); Chauri Chaura - NCM withdrawn.

s: Where and when was the Satyagraha Sabha established?
x: The Satyagraha Sabha was formed in Bombay in February 1919, using the networks of the Home Rule League.

s: On which date was the hartal called by Gandhi against the Rowlatt Act observed?
x: Gandhi called a nationwide hartal for 6 April 1919, involving fasting, prayer and protest against the Act.

s: Why did Gandhi withdraw the Rowlatt Satyagraha on 18 April 1919?
o: Acceptance of Congress demands by the Hunter Committee
Advice of the Home Rule League
x: The movement turned violent in Punjab and Ahmedabad, so Gandhi called it a Himalayan blunder and withdrew it on 18 April 1919.

s: Who translated Mahatma Gandhi's speech at Vijayawada on 8 April 1919?
x: Gandhi visited Vijayawada on 8 April 1919, and Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao translated his speech.

s: Which Andhra newspapers opposed the Rowlatt Act?
x: Andhra Patrika and Krishna Patrika opposed the Act.

s: Under whose leadership did the Guntur Bar Association demand the jailing of General Dyer?
x: The Guntur Bar Association, led by Konda Venkatappayya, demanded that General Dyer be jailed.

s: Which district conferences of Andhra condemned the Jallianwala Bagh massacre?
x: The Ganjam, Godavari and Krishna district conferences condemned the massacre.

s: Who suggested a no-tax campaign against the Rowlatt Act?
x: Swami Shraddhanand suggested a no-tax campaign as part of the Rowlatt protest.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Rowlatt Satyagraha in Andhra:
1. The hartal of 6 April 1919 was observed peacefully at Vizag, Rajahmundry, Guntur, Vijayawada and Nellore.
2. Gandhi addressed a meeting at Vijayawada on 8 April 1919.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Andhra towns observed peaceful hartals on 6 April 1919, and Gandhi spoke at Vijayawada on 8 April 1919.

s: Which Andhra leader demanded fundamental rights at a meeting in Nellore in September 1919?
x: After the massacre, Prakasam demanded fundamental rights at a Nellore meeting in September 1919.

s: The Rowlatt Satyagraha of 1919 was India's first all-India campaign of which kind?
x: The Rowlatt Satyagraha was the first all-India mass strike and was urban-centred, not confined to rural Punjab.

s: Which of the following was an Indian member of the Hunter Committee?
x: Chimanlal Setalvad, Jagat Narayan and Sultan Ahmed Khan were the Indian members; their minority report was more critical of Dyer.

s: What was the outcome of the Hunter Committee inquiry for General Dyer?
o: He was fully exonerated and retained in command
He was censured and relieved of command but received no real punishment
He was sentenced to life imprisonment
He was promoted to Lieutenant Governor of Punjab
x: Dyer was censured and relieved of command but not really punished; the House of Lords backed him and Gandhi called the findings a whitewash.

s: Who among the following was a member of the Congress's Punjab Sub-Committee that inquired into the Punjab events?
x: The Punjab Sub-Committee comprised Motilal Nehru, C.R. Das, Abbas Tyabji, M.R. Jayakar and Gandhi; the other three were Indian members of the official Hunter Committee.

s: How did the Hunter Committee describe General Dyer's action?
x: The Hunter Committee criticised Dyer by calling his action an 'error of judgement'; 'preventive murder' was Montagu's phrase.

s: What was the official name of the Hunter Committee?
x: The Hunter Committee was the Disorders Inquiry Committee, set up on 14 October 1919.

s: How many of the Hunter Committee's eight members were Indians?
x: It had 8 members: 5 British and 3 Indian.

s: Who wrote the minority report of the Hunter Committee, which was more critical of Dyer?
x: Setalvad, Jagat Narayan and Sultan Ahmed Khan wrote the minority report; the five British members wrote the majority report.

s: Besides the Jallianwala Bagh massacre, the Hunter Committee inquired into disturbances in which places?
o: Sind, Baluchistan and the North-West Frontier
x: The Hunter (Disorders Inquiry) Committee probed Jallianwala Bagh and the disturbances in Bombay, Delhi and Punjab.

s: When was the Hunter Committee set up?
x: The Hunter Committee was set up on 14 October 1919.

s: How did Gandhi describe the findings of the Hunter Committee?
x: Gandhi called the Hunter findings a 'whitewash'; 'error of judgement' was the committee's own phrase for Dyer's act.

s: Which of the following was NOT a member of the Congress's Punjab Sub-Committee?
x: Setalvad was an Indian member of the official Hunter Committee; the Congress committee had Motilal Nehru, C.R. Das, Tyabji, Jayakar and Gandhi.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Congress inquiry into the Punjab events:
1. It called the firing inhuman.
2. It described Dyer's action as 'an error of judgement'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Congress report called the firing inhuman; 'an error of judgement' was the Hunter Committee's verdict.

s: Of which body was Abbas Tyabji a member?
x: Abbas Tyabji sat on the Congress's non-official Punjab Sub-Committee.

s: Where did Udham Singh assassinate Michael O'Dwyer on 13 March 1940?
x: Udham Singh killed Michael O'Dwyer at Caxton Hall, London, on 13 March 1940.

s: On which date was the Bardoli resolution, by which the Non-Cooperation Movement was withdrawn, adopted?
x: The Bardoli resolution of 11–12 February 1922 turned the Congress towards constructive work after the movement was withdrawn.

s: Who called the withdrawal of the Non-Cooperation Movement after Chauri Chaura a 'national calamity'?
x: Subhas Chandra Bose called the withdrawal a national calamity; M.N. Roy described it as weak leadership.

s: How many policemen were killed when a crowd burnt the police station at Chauri Chaura in February 1922?
x: At Chauri Chaura in Gorakhpur district (4 February 1922), the crowd burnt the police station and 22 policemen were killed; the NCM was then withdrawn by the Bardoli resolution.

s:
Arrange in chronological order:
A. Moplah uprising
B. Prince of Wales boycott
C. Chauri Chaura incident
D. Formation of the Swaraj Party
x: Moplah uprising (August 1921), Prince of Wales boycott (17 November 1921), Chauri Chaura (February 1922), Swaraj Party (1923).

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the events of 1921-23?
o: The Prince of Wales boycott (17 November 1921) came before the Bardoli resolution
The Bardoli resolution (11-12 February 1922) came before Gandhi's arrest
The Swaraj Party was formed before the Bardoli resolution
Gandhi was arrested in March 1922, before the Swaraj Party was formed
x: The Swaraj Party was formed in 1923, after the Bardoli resolution (February 1922) and Gandhi's arrest (March 1922).

s: According to the Marxist interpretation, Gandhi withdrew the Non-Cooperation Movement to prevent which of the following?
o: A radical anti-landlord turn of the movement
The expansion of council entry by Swarajists
The formation of the Akali Dal
x: The Marxist interpretation argued that Gandhi halted the movement to prevent it from taking a radical anti-landlord direction.

s: How many people were finally hanged in the Chauri Chaura case?
x: The Gorakhpur Sessions Judge sentenced 172 to death, but 19 were finally hanged (1923).

s: At Chauri Chaura, the crowd was protesting the arrest of its leader while campaigning against which of the following?
x: The crowd protested the arrest of its leader in the anti-liquor campaign; after police firing it burnt the police station.

s: Which leader criticised the withdrawal of the NCM as showing weak leadership?
x: M.N. Roy blamed weak leadership; Bose called it a 'national calamity'.

s: Who defended the accused of the Chauri Chaura incident in court?
x: Madan Mohan Malaviya defended the Chauri Chaura accused; 172 were sentenced to death and 19 were finally hanged.

s: Which incident took place on 4 February 1922 in Gorakhpur district of Uttar Pradesh?
x: On 4 February 1922 a crowd burnt the police station at Chauri Chaura in Gorakhpur district, UP, killing 22 policemen.

s: Where was the AICC meeting of 24 February 1922, at which Dr. Moonje moved a censure vote against Gandhi, held?
x: The censure vote against Gandhi for calling off the NCM was moved by Dr. Moonje at the AICC in Delhi on 24 February 1922.

s: How many accused in the Chauri Chaura case were sentenced to death by the Gorakhpur Sessions Judge?
x: The Sessions Judge sentenced 172 to death; finally 19 were hanged.

s: Who reacted to the suspension of the Non-Cooperation Movement with 'amazement and consternation'?
x: Jawaharlal Nehru reacted with 'amazement and consternation'; Bose called it a national tragedy and M.N. Roy blamed weak leadership.

s: Who called the suspension of the NCM a 'national tragedy'?
x: Subhas Bose called it a 'national tragedy'; Nehru reacted with 'amazement and consternation'.

s: Why did Gandhi suspend the Non-Cooperation Movement in February 1922?
o: Failure to meet the Bezawada targets
Boycott of the Prince of Wales visit
x: The NCM was suspended at Bardoli (11-12 February 1922) because of the violence at Chauri Chaura.

s: The Khilafat leaders opposed which treaty imposed on the Ottoman Empire after the First World War?
x: The Treaty of Sevres (May 1920) threatened the territorial integrity of the Ottoman Empire and intensified the Khilafat agitation.

s: Which one of the following was NOT associated with the Khilafat Movement?
x: Tej Bahadur Sapru was not a Khilafat leader; he is known as a mediator of the Gandhi-Irwin Pact (1931). Hakim Ajmal Khan, Hasrat Mohani and Dr. M.A. Ansari were Khilafat leaders along with the Ali brothers and Abul Kalam Azad.

s: In which year did Turkey abolish the Caliphate, ending the relevance of the Khilafat agitation?
x: Turkey abolished the Caliphate in 1924, removing the central issue around which the Khilafat agitation had developed.

s: At which of the following did Gandhi preside and first propose non-violent non-cooperation over the Khilafat issue?
x: Gandhi presided over the All-India Khilafat Conference at Delhi in November 1919 and first proposed non-violent non-cooperation there. The Allahabad conference (June 1920) endorsed the boycott and asked him to lead; Nagpur (Dec 1920) formally adopted the NCM; the Karachi conference (July 1921) urged Muslims to quit the Army.

s: The Khilafat–Non-Cooperation phase is regarded as the high point of which of the following?
x: The Khilafat–Non-Cooperation phase represented the high point of Hindu-Muslim unity during the national movement.

s: In which year was the Khilafat Committee formed?
x: The Khilafat Committee was organised in 1919 to protect the Ottoman Khalifa.

s: At the Karachi Khilafat conference of July 1921, the Ali brothers urged Muslims to quit which of the following?
x: At Karachi (July 1921) the Ali brothers, Muhammad Ali and Shaukat Ali, urged Muslims to quit the Army.

s: Which Khilafat leader gave up the title 'Haziq-ul-Mulk'?
x: Hakim Ajmal Khan gave up the title Haziq-ul-Mulk during the Khilafat-Non-Cooperation phase.

s: Who coined the slogan 'Inquilab Zindabad'?
x: Hasrat Mohani coined 'Inquilab Zindabad' and proposed Swaraj as complete independence at Ahmedabad (1921).

s: Gandhi supported the Khilafat cause chiefly as an opportunity to forge which of the following?
x: Gandhi merged the Khilafat cause with Swaraj and regarded it as an opportunity to forge Hindu-Muslim unity.

s: In support of whom was the Khilafat Movement organised?
x: The Khilafat Movement aimed to protect the Ottoman Sultan as Khalifa (Caliph) and the territory of the Ottoman Empire.

s: Which of the following leaders did NOT support the Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement?
x: M.A. Jinnah did not support the movement; the others were Khilafat leaders.

s: Which of the following gave up legal practice during the Non-Cooperation Movement?
x: T. Prakasam was among the lawyers who gave up practice, along with Motilal Nehru, C.R. Das, Rajagopalachari, Patel and others; Ambedkar was not.

s: To which region did Saifuddin Kitchlew, who gave up legal practice during the NCM, belong?
x: Saifuddin Kitchlew of Punjab gave up his practice during the NCM.

s: In which case had C.R. Das earlier defended Aurobindo?
x: C.R. Das, a Bengal lawyer, had defended Aurobindo in the Alipore Bomb Case.

s: Which of the following did NOT give up legal practice during the Non-Cooperation Movement?
x: Prakasam, Rajendra Prasad and Asaf Ali gave up practice; Ambedkar was not among them.

s: Which English paper is associated with Motilal Nehru?
x: Motilal Nehru ran the English paper The Independent.

s: In which year was the Sikh Gurdwaras Act, the result of the Akali Movement for gurdwara reform, passed?
x: The Akali Movement (1920–25) against corrupt mahants culminated in the Sikh Gurdwaras Act, 1925.

s: Which of the following mainly took part in the Moplah uprising of 1921 in Malabar, Kerala?
o: Tribal forest users against British forest officials
x: The Moplah uprising took place in Malabar, Kerala, and began as an agrarian conflict involving Muslim tenants and Hindu landlords before turning communal.

s: On which date did the Prince of Wales, whose visit was boycotted during the NCM, land at Bombay?
x: He landed at Bombay on 17 November 1921, met by a nationwide hartal and clashes in Bombay.

s: Against which of the following was the Akali movement of 1920-25 directed?
x: The Akalis sought gurdwara reform against corrupt mahants, leading to the Sikh Gurdwaras Act, 1925.

s: In which year did the Moplah uprising take place in Malabar?
x: The Moplah (Mappila) uprising broke out in Malabar, Kerala, in August 1921.

s: With which incident of 1921 is the Akali movement associated?
x: The Akali movement (1920-25) for gurdwara reform saw the Nankana Sahib incident in 1921.

s: Who presided over the Nagpur session of the Indian National Congress in December 1920?
x: C. Vijayaraghavachariar presided over the Nagpur session of the Congress in December 1920.

s: Who presided over the Amritsar session of the Congress (1919), which called the Montagu-Chelmsford reforms inadequate and disappointing?
x: The Amritsar session of 1919 was presided over by Motilal Nehru.

s: At the Calcutta special session, which of the following Andhra leaders initially opposed the Non-Cooperation resolution but later resigned from the Madras Legislature?
x: Konda Venkatappayya initially opposed the resolution but subsequently resigned from the Madras Legislature. Pattabhi Sitaramayya, Duggirala, A. Kaleswara Rao and Peta Bapayya were also among the Andhra participants.

s: Which Congress session is associated with Mahatma Gandhi’s only presidency of the Indian National Congress?
x: Mahatma Gandhi presided over the Belgaum Session in 1924, which was his only presidency of the Indian National Congress.

s:
Assertion (A): The Nagpur session of the Congress (December 1920) organised Provincial Congress Committees on linguistic lines.
Reason (R): The Nagpur session fixed the Congress membership fee at one rupee.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
x: The Nagpur session reorganised Congress units on linguistic lines, but the membership fee was fixed at four annas, not one rupee.

s: Who presided over the Calcutta special session of the Congress (September 1920) that approved non-cooperation?
x: Lala Lajpat Rai presided over the Calcutta special session, where Gandhi's resolution passed 1886 to 884.

s: What was the Congress membership fee fixed at under the constitution adopted at Nagpur (1920)?
x: The Nagpur constitution fixed the membership fee at four annas, not one rupee.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Nagpur session (1920):
1. It set up an AICC of 350 members.
2. It organised Provincial Congress Committees on linguistic lines.
3. It was presided over by Lala Lajpat Rai.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Nagpur created a 350-member AICC and linguistic PCCs; it was presided over by C. Vijayaraghavachariar, not Lajpat Rai.

s: Which session of the Indian National Congress was presided over by C.R. Das?
x: C.R. Das presided over the Gaya session of December 1922, where his council-entry plan was rejected.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: C.R. Das — Bengal lawyer who gave up practice
Lala Lajpat Rai — President of the Gaya session
x: C.R. Das, not Lala Lajpat Rai, was associated with the Gaya presidency. Lala Lajpat Rai presided over the Calcutta special session.

s: Which of the following was a background factor behind the launch of the Non-Cooperation Movement?
x: The Khilafat issue, along with the Rowlatt Act and the Jallianwala Bagh massacre, was a cause of the movement; the Simon Commission Report was not.

s: The Non-Cooperation Movement was launched on 1 August 1920, the day of whose death?
x: The movement was launched on 1 August 1920, the day Tilak died; the Calcutta special session approved it in September 1920.

s: Which of the following was NOT a cause of the Non-Cooperation Movement?
x: The Simon Commission came after the NCM (1920-22), so it could not be a cause; Rowlatt Act, Jallianwala Bagh and Khilafat were causes.

s: On the day the NCM was launched (1 August 1920), Gandhi returned which medal?
o: Order of the Star of India
x: On 1 August 1920 Gandhi returned his Kaiser-i-Hind medal as the NCM began.

s: Within what period did Gandhi promise Swaraj if the non-cooperation programme was followed?
x: Gandhi promised Swaraj within a year if non-cooperation was followed.

s: By what vote was Gandhi's non-cooperation resolution passed at the Calcutta special session (1920)?
x: The resolution was carried 1886 to 884; C.R. Das opposed it there.

s: Which leader opposed Gandhi's non-cooperation resolution at the Calcutta special session of 1920?
x: C.R. Das opposed the resolution at Calcutta; it was still passed by 1886 to 884 votes.

s: Under the Non-Cooperation programme, how were the November 1920 legislative elections treated?
x: The November 1920 elections were boycotted; surrender of titles and non-payment of taxes (as the final stage) were part of the programme.

s: Which of the following was part of the constructive programme of the Non-Cooperation Movement?
o: Promotion of khadi and the charkha
x: Promotion of khadi and the charkha was constructive work; boycott of foreign cloth was a boycott measure.

s: Which of the following was NOT part of the NCM programme?
x: The programme asked for surrender of titles; retention of titles was not part of it.

s: Under the NCM programme, by what were government law courts to be replaced?
x: The programme called for boycott of law courts and settlement of disputes in panchayat courts.

s: What was the target of the Tilak Swaraj Fund associated with the Non-Cooperation Movement?
x: The Tilak Swaraj Fund had a target and collection of one crore rupees.

s: Which of the following institutions was founded at Aligarh in 1920 and later shifted to Delhi?
x: Jamia Millia Islamia was founded at Aligarh in 1920 and later shifted to Delhi.

s: In which year did Sir Syed Ahmad Khan establish the MAO College, from which Aligarh Muslim University developed?
x: The MAO College was established in 1875; the university got legal status in 1920 but was not a Non-Cooperation national institution.

s: In which year was Gujarat Vidyapith, a national institution of the Non-Cooperation era, founded?
x: Gujarat Vidyapith was founded in 1920, while Kashi and Bihar Vidyapiths came in 1921.

s: In which year was Kashi Vidyapith at Varanasi founded?
x: Kashi Vidyapith, Varanasi, was founded in 1921 during the NCM.

s: In which year was Besant Theosophical College, Madanapalle, which was NOT an NCM institution, founded?
x: Annie Besant founded the college at Madanapalle in 1915, before the NCM.

s: About how many national schools and colleges came up during the Non-Cooperation Movement?
x: About 800 national schools and colleges were started during the NCM.

s: Which national institution did Jai Prakash Narayan join after leaving Patna College during the Non-Cooperation Movement?
x: JP left Patna College with 20 days left for exams and joined Bihar Vidyapeeth.

s: Where was Bihar Vidyapith, a national institution of the Non-Cooperation era, founded in 1921?
x: Bihar Vidyapith was founded at Patna in 1921.

s: Which leader opposed the boycott of schools during the Non-Cooperation Movement?
x: Lala Lajpat Rai opposed the boycott of schools, though he presided over the Calcutta special session.

s: In April 1919, while on his way to Punjab, Gandhi was stopped and detained by the British at:
x: In April 1919 Gandhi was stopped and detained at Palwal while proceeding towards Punjab; the incident contributed to riots.

s: What sentence was Gandhi given in the Great Trial at Ahmedabad (March 1922)?
x: Charged with sedition under Section 124A for his Young India articles, Gandhi received a six-year sentence.

s: Which judge presided over Gandhi's Great Trial of 1922?
x: Judge C.N. Broomfield presided over the Great Trial on 18 March 1922, where Gandhi pleaded guilty and asked for the highest penalty.

s: Which of the following periodicals was NOT edited by Gandhi?
x: The Bengalee was not Gandhi's paper; it was Surendranath Banerjea's. Gandhi's papers were Young India, Navajivan, Indian Opinion and Harijan.

s: Where was Gandhi arrested on 10 March 1922?
x: Gandhi was arrested at Sabarmati, Ahmedabad, on 10 March 1922.

s: Gandhi was charged with sedition in 1922 under which section of the IPC?
x: He was charged under Section 124A IPC for three articles in Young India.

s: In which paper were articles such as 'Tampering with Loyalty', on which Gandhi's 1922 sedition charge rested, published?
x: The charge was based on three Young India articles, including 'Tampering with Loyalty' and 'Shaking the Manes'.

s: What did Gandhi do at the Great Trial of 1922?
o: Pleaded guilty and asked for the highest penalty
x: Gandhi pleaded guilty before Judge Broomfield and asked for the highest penalty; he got 6 years.

s: In which year was Gandhi, sentenced to six years in 1922, released?
x: He was released in 1924 on health grounds.

s: On which date did Gandhi's Great Trial take place at Ahmedabad?
x: Gandhi was arrested on 10 March 1922 and tried at Ahmedabad on 18 March 1922.

s: The Non-Cooperation Movement, the first nationwide mass movement, made which body a mass force for the first time?
x: Swaraj was not won within one year, but the NCM made the Indian National Congress a mass force for the first time.

s: During the Non-Cooperation Movement, tribals and forest users took part by opposing which of the following?
x: Tribals and forest users joined the movement by opposing pullari, while peasants joined no-tax campaigns.

s: The Palnadu satyagraha involved refusal to pay which tax?
x: The Palnadu forest satyagraha involved refusal to pay the pullari, or grazing, tax and a boycott of forest officials.

s: The Chirala-Perala Movement opposed the formation of which of the following?
x: The Chirala-Perala Movement opposed turning Chirala into a municipality, which brought heavy taxes. Under Duggirala Gopalakrishnaiah, residents moved out to Ramnagar.

s: Which of the following pairs of movement and leader is correctly matched?
x: Kanneganti Hanumanthu led the Palnadu forest satyagraha; Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya led Chirala-Perala and Parvataneni Veeraiah Chowdary led Pedanandipadu.

s: Which one of the following pairs of a volunteer force and the Andhra leader associated with it is correctly matched?
x: Parvataneni Veeraiah Chowdary, leader of the Pedanandipadu no-tax campaign, founded the Shanti Sena. The Ramadandu was Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya's volunteer force at Chirala-Perala; Kanneganti Hanumanthu led the Palnadu pullari satyagraha.

s: The volunteer force 'Ramadandu' was associated with which movement?
x: Ramadandu was Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya's volunteer force in the Chirala-Perala movement; Shanti Sena belonged to Pedanandipadu.

s: Who led the Palnadu forest satyagraha?
x: Kanneganti Hanumanthu led the Palnadu forest satyagraha, which involved boycotting forest officials and refusing the grazing tax.

s: Who led the no-tax campaign at Pedanandipadu during the Non-Cooperation Movement?
x: Parvataneni Veerayya Chowdary led the Pedanandipadu no-tax campaign (1921-22) and founded the Shanti Sena.

s: In which year was Kanneganti Hanumanthu killed in police firing during the Palnadu satyagraha?
x: The Palnadu pullari satyagraha ran in 1921-22; Kanneganti Hanumanthu was killed in police firing in 1922.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The forest satyagraha in Andhra first started in Palnadu.
2. The Palnadu satyagraha was a refusal to pay the pullari (grazing) tax.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: the forest satyagraha first began in Palnadu, where people refused the pullari tax.

s: The Guntur no-tax campaign was suspended on 11 February 1922 after Gandhi sent a message to which leader?
x: After Chauri Chaura, Gandhi's message to Konda Venkatappayya led to the suspension of the Guntur no-tax campaign.

s: In which taluka of Guntur district did the Chirala-Perala movement take place?
x: Chirala-Perala was in Bapatla taluka of Guntur district.

s: The Chirala-Perala, Pedanandipadu and Palnadu episodes of the NCM were all in which old district?
x: All three main NCM episodes of Andhra were in the old Guntur district.

s: During the Chirala-Perala movement, where did the residents who left the town live in a camp?
x: Opposing the new municipality and its taxes, residents moved to a camp at Ramnagar.

s: What did the Pedanandipadu campaign of 1921-22 refuse to pay?
x: Pedanandipadu villages refused land revenue under Parvataneni Veerayya Chowdary.

s: Who wrote the play *Nayakuralu* while in jail in connection with the Palnadu agitation?
x: Unnava Lakshmi Narayana wrote the play *Nayakuralu* while he was in jail.

s:
Consider the following about the Palnadu forest satyagraha:
1. Unnava Lakshmi Narayana and Madabhushi Vedantam Narasimhachari studied and supported it.
2. Konda Venkatappayya tried to moderate it, as the Congress favoured social boycott rather than tax refusal.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: Unnava Lakshmi Narayana and Madabhushi Vedantam Narasimhachari backed the movement, while Konda Venkatappayya tried to moderate it because the Congress favoured social boycott over tax refusal.

s: During the Palnadu Pullari satyagraha, where were the 300 cattle driven into the forest without paying the tax impounded?
x: The cattle were impounded at Minchalapadu; Macherla was where officials were socially boycotted.

s: Kanneganti Hanumanthu was killed in police firing during which incident?
o: The boycott of the Prince of Wales at Vijayawada
x: Kanneganti Hanumanthu was shot dead in the cattle-rescue action at Minchalapadu on 22 February 1922. The cattle had been impounded there; Macherla was where officials were socially boycotted.

s: Under the Forest Act of 1878, how much was the Pullari tax on a cow?
x: Pullari was 12 annas per cow and Rs 1.50 per buffalo.

s: Where did the social boycott of forest officials take place in the Palnadu satyagraha?
x: Officials were socially boycotted at Macherla; the cattle were impounded at Minchalapadu.

s: Which Congress leader tried to dilute the Palnadu struggle, preferring social boycott to tax refusal?
x: Konda Venkatappayya tried to calm the struggle; Congress preferred social boycott, not tax refusal.

s: On which date was Kanneganti Hanumanthu shot dead at Minchalapadu?
x: He was shot dead in the cattle-rescue action at Minchalapadu on 22 February 1922.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Palnad forest satyagraha:
1. It took place in 1921-22.
2. It was the first forest satyagraha in Andhra.
3. It took place in Nellore district.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Palnad satyagraha (1921-22) was the first forest satyagraha in Andhra; Palnadu is in Guntur district, not Nellore.

s: In which district was Kanneganti Hanumanthu, the hero of the Palnadu satyagraha, born?
x: Kanneganti Hanumanthu was born in Guntur district, where the Palnadu struggle took place.

s: Where did the Forest Satyagraha first start?
x: The Forest Satyagraha during the Non-Cooperation Movement first started in Palnadu in Guntur district. Chintapalli belongs to Alluri's revolt and Bapatla to the first Andhra Mahasabha.

s: Gandhi's visit to Kakinada in April 1921 inspired which later national leader?
x: Gandhi's Kakinada visit in April 1921 inspired Durgabai Deshmukh.

s: The AICC meeting at Vijayawada (1921) set a target of how many charkhas?
x: The Vijayawada targets were one crore rupees for the Tilak Swaraj Fund, one crore members and twenty lakh charkhas.

s: Who presented a design for the national flag at the AICC meeting held at Vijayawada in 1921?
x: Pingali Venkayya presented his flag design at the Vijayawada AICC meeting.

s: After the Congress boycotted the November 1920 elections in Madras Presidency, who formed the first ministry?
x: The Justice Party won 63 of 98 seats and the first ministry was formed under A. Subbarayalu Reddiar on 17 December 1920.

s: After the Congress boycott of the November 1920 elections, the Justice Party won how many of 98 seats in Madras?
x: The Justice Party won 63 of 98 seats and formed the first ministry under A. Subbarayalu Reddiar.

s: What target of Congress membership was set at the AICC meeting at Vijayawada in 1921?
x: The Vijayawada AICC set targets of 1 crore members, Rs 1 crore for the Tilak Swaraj Fund and 20 lakh charkhas.

s: At which levels did the APCC meeting at Vijayawada in January 1921 set up Congress committees?
x: After Nagpur, the APCC met at Vijayawada in January 1921 and set up district, taluk and village committees.

s:
Consider the following statements about Vijayawada in 1921:
1. The APCC met there in January 1921.
2. The AICC met there in March-April 1921.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: the APCC met in January 1921 and the AICC session followed on 31 March - 1 April 1921; they are different meetings.

s: The AICC meeting held at Vijayawada in 1921 is particularly associated with which decision?
o: Acceptance of Gandhi's leadership of the national struggle
Formation of the Swaraj Party at Gaya
Approval of council entry as the sole Congress programme
x: At the 1921 AICC meeting at Vijayawada, political leaders accepted Gandhi's leadership of the national struggle.

s: What did the flag design of Pingali Venkayya, endorsed by Gandhi at the Vijayawada AICC meeting (1921), carry?
x: Pingali Venkayya's design endorsed by Gandhi at Vijayawada had the charkha.

s: Pingali Venkayya was born at which place?
x: Pingali Venkayya was born at Bhatlapenumarru.

s: The AICC at Vijayawada (1921) set a target of how many charkhas?
x: The targets were 1 crore members, Rs 1 crore for the Tilak Swaraj Fund and 20 lakh charkhas.

s: By which date were the targets set at the Vijayawada AICC (1921) to be met?
x: The targets of members, funds and charkhas were to be met by 30 June 1921.

s: How much money was the Tilak Swaraj Fund to raise under the targets set by the AICC at Vijayawada (1921)?
x: The Vijayawada AICC fixed Rs 1 crore for the Tilak Swaraj Fund, with 1 crore members and 20 lakh charkhas.

s: How many Congress members did the AICC at Vijayawada (1921) aim to enrol by 30 June 1921?
x: The target was 1 crore Congress members by 30 June 1921.

s: On whose 150th birth anniversary did the Prime Minister pay tribute in August 2026?
x: The PM paid tribute to Pingali Venkayya, designer of the flag shown at Vijayawada in 1921, on his 150th birth anniversary (3 August 2026).

s: Which group of women leaders emerged prominently in Andhra during Gandhi's Non-Cooperation tour?
o: Duvvuri Subbamma, Ponaka Kanakamma and Unnava Lakshmibayamma
Durgabai, Annie Besant and Sarojini Naidu
Ponaka Kanakamma, Konda Venkatappayya and Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya
Unnava Lakshmibayamma, Garimella Satyanarayana and Durgabai
x: Duvvuri Subbamma, Ponaka Kanakamma and Unnava Lakshmibayamma emerged as women leaders during this phase of the movement.

s: During Gandhi's April 1921 tour of coastal Andhra, who translated his speech at Kakinada and donated Rs 5,000?
x: At Kakinada (April 1921) Durgabai translated Gandhi's speech and gave Rs 5,000. Duvvuri Subbamma, Ponaka Kanakamma and Unnava Lakshmibayamma were women leaders who emerged in the same phase, but the Kakinada translation is linked to Durgabai.

s: Which places did Gandhi's October 1921 tour of Andhra, the peak of the NCM there, cover?
x: The October 1921 tour covered Kurnool, Kadapa, Tirupati and Tadipatri; the April tour was coastal.

s: Which of the following was NOT visited in Gandhi's April 1921 coastal tour of Andhra?
x: Kurnool was covered in the October 1921 tour; Kakinada, Machilipatnam and Rajahmundry were in the April tour.

s: Which of the following places was covered in Gandhi's October 1921 tour of Andhra?
x: In October 1921 Gandhi toured Kurnool, Kadapa, Tirupati and Tadipatri; Kakinada, Eluru and Machilipatnam were on his April coastal tour.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched with the legacy of the Non-Cooperation Movement in Andhra?
x: The National College was established at Eluru, not Tadipatri. Pallepadu Ashram was in Nellore and Seethanagaram Ashram was near Rajahmundry.

s: Which statement regarding the Seethanagaram Ashram is correct?
o: It was at Chirala and was known as Andhra Vidyapeetha Goshthi.
It was at Nellore and was known as Pallepadu Ashram.
It was at Eluru and became the National College.
It was near Rajahmundry and is now known as Kasturba Ashram.
x: The Seethanagaram Ashram was located near Rajahmundry and is now known as Kasturba Ashram.

s: Pallepadu Ashram of the NCM era was in which district?
x: Pallepadu Ashram was in Nellore; Seethanagaram Ashram was near Rajahmundry.

s: Where was Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya's Andhra Vidyapeetha Goshthi?
x: The Andhra Vidyapeetha Goshthi of Duggirala was at Chirala.

s: Where was the National College of the NCM era in Andhra?
x: Eluru had the National College, not Tadipatri.

s: Which place in Andhra was famous for its khadi during the Non-Cooperation era?
x: Ponduru was famous for khadi; Eluru had the National College and Pallepadu an ashram.

s: On 5 November 1921, the Delhi AICC permitted provinces to launch which form of action?
x: The Delhi AICC of 5 November 1921 permitted provinces to launch civil disobedience, including no-tax campaigns.

s: On which date did the Delhi AICC that allowed provinces to start civil disobedience, including no-tax campaigns, meet?
x: The Delhi AICC of 5 November 1921 permitted civil disobedience, including no-tax campaigns.

s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
1. APCC meeting at Vijayawada
2. Boycott of the Prince of Wales visit
3. Chauri Chaura incident
4. AICC meeting at Bezawada
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: APCC met in January 1921, the Bezawada AICC in March-April 1921, the Prince of Wales boycott was in November 1921 and Chauri Chaura in February 1922.

s: Who founded the Home Rule League, whose Andhra branches were started under Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao?
x: Annie Besant founded the Home Rule Movement in 1916; its Andhra branches were started under Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao.

s: Who served as secretary of the Andhra division of the Home Rule League?
x: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao was secretary of the Andhra division, with branches at Guntur, Vijayawada and Kakinada.

s: With whom was the newspaper Krishna Patrika associated?
x: Krishna Patrika was associated with Mutnuri; Desamata was associated with Chilakamarti.

s: What were the protests held at Tenali and Vijayawada after Annie Besant's arrest called?
x: The protests at Tenali and Vijayawada following Besant's arrest were called “Confinement Day” protests.

s: Under what title did Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao translate Sarojini Naidu's 'Awake Mother'?
x: He translated Awake Mother as Nuthana Haindava Matrigeetham; Swarajya Paramoddesham was a Telugu pamphlet.

s: The demand raised by the Andhra delegation before Montagu in December 1917 primarily concerned:
o: The transfer of the capital to Delhi
The formation of the Swarajya Sabha
x: The Montagu Declaration raised hopes of a separate Andhra province, and an Andhra delegation led by Nyapati Subba Rao met Montagu on 20 December 1917 to press that demand.

s: By 1917, how many Home Rule branches had been set up in Andhra?
x: Andhra had 52 Home Rule branches by 1917; about 200 was the figure for Besant's whole League.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Desamata was edited by Chilakamarti; Krishna Patrika was Mutnuri Krishna Rao's, The Leader Malaviya's and Bombay Chronicle Pherozeshah Mehta's.

s: Who organised Annie Besant's tour of Kakinada, Rajahmundry and Eluru after the Lucknow session of 1916?
x: Besant's Andhra tour after Lucknow (1916) was organised by Mocherla Hanumantha Rao.

s: Who led the Andhra delegation that met Montagu on 20 December 1917 for a separate Andhra province?
x: On 20 December 1917 an Andhra delegation under Nyapati Subba Rao asked Montagu for a separate Andhra province.

s: What was the name of the Telugu pamphlet used for Home Rule propaganda in Andhra?
x: Home Rule workers in Andhra spread Telugu pamphlets such as Swarajya Paramoddesham.

s: Who toured Kakinada, Rajahmundry and Eluru after the Lucknow session of 1916?
x: Annie Besant toured Andhra (Kakinada, Rajahmundry, Eluru) after the Lucknow session.

s: By 1917, how many Home Rule branches did Andhra have?
x: Andhra had 52 Home Rule branches by 1917.

s: After Annie Besant's arrest in June 1917, students of which Andhra college wore 'Besant lockets'?
x: Students of the Machilipatnam National College wore Besant lockets after her arrest on 15 June 1917.

s: Who became the first woman President of the Indian National Congress, in 1917?
x: Annie Besant presided over the Congress in 1917 and was its first woman President. Sarojini Naidu (1925) was the first Indian woman President; Nellie Sengupta presided later (1933); Kasturba Gandhi never presided.

s: Who was the secretary of the Andhra division of the Home Rule League?
x: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao was secretary of the Andhra division and led the opening of its branches.

s: Where was the Home Rule flag of 5 red and 4 green stripes hoisted in 1917?
x: The Home Rule flag was hoisted at Coimbatore in 1917.

s: Who was the first Indian woman President of the INC?
x: Sarojini Naidu (1925) was the first Indian woman President; Annie Besant (1917) was the first woman President.

s: In 1919, Andhra nationalists meeting at Vijayawada resolved that who should represent India at the Paris Peace Conference?
x: At Vijayawada in 1919 Andhra nationalists resolved that Tilak should represent India at the Paris Peace Conference.

s: Who among the following women presided over the Indian National Congress in 1933?
x: Nellie Sengupta presided in 1933, after Annie Besant (1917) and Sarojini Naidu (1925).

s: Who wrote the song 'Veeragandhamu Techhinaramu'?
x: Veeragandhamu Techhinaramu was written by Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary.

s: Which of the following pairs of work and author is correctly matched?
x: Makoddi Telladoratanam was by Garimella Satyanarayana and Veeragandhamu Techhinaramu by Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary; the banned play Viplava Parivarthanam is credited in the notes to Kodali Anjaneyulu.

s: Who wrote the banned play 'Viplava Parivarthanam'?
x: The banned play Viplava Parivarthanam is credited to Kodali Anjaneyulu (some keys give Gollapudi Sitarama Sastri). Tripuraneni wrote Veeragandhamu Techhinaramu and Garimella Makoddi Telladoratanam.

s: Who is known as 'Andhra Shivaji'?
x: Parvataneni Veerayya Chowdary, leader of the Pedanandipadu no-tax campaign, was called 'Andhra Shivaji'.

s: Which of the following pairs of leader and title is correctly matched?
x: Konda Venkatappaiah was known as Desabhakta; Duggirala was Andhra Ratna, Prakasam was Andhra Kesari and Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao was Desoddharaka.

s: Who among the following was given the title 'Desoddharaka'?
x: Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao was 'Desoddharaka'; Konda Venkatappaiah was 'Desabhakta'.

s: Who was given the title 'Andhra Ratna'?
x: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya was called Andhra Ratna; Prakasam was Andhra Kesari.

s: Which leader of the Non-Cooperation era was associated with Madras and later became a No-Changer?
x: Rajagopalachari (Madras) became a No-Changer; C.R. Das (Bengal) and Motilal Nehru (UP) became Swarajists.

s: After the withdrawal of the Non-Cooperation Movement, what did the pro-changers favour?
x: The pro-changers, or Swarajists, sought to enter the councils to 'end or mend' them; the no-changers preferred constructive work and continued boycott.

s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Andhra branch of the Swaraj Party?
o: Pithapuram Raja was president and C.R. Das was secretary.
V. Ramadas was president and Motilal Nehru was secretary.
Unava Lakshmi Narayana was president and Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao was secretary.
Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao was president and Unava Lakshmi Narayana was secretary.
x: The Andhra branch had Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao as president and Unava Lakshmi Narayana as secretary.

s: Who founded the Congress-Khilafat Swaraj Party along with C.R. Das?
x: C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru were the principal founders of the Swaraj Party; Jawaharlal Nehru was not a founder.

s: With which strategy of the Swarajists was the expression 'End or Mend' associated?
o: forming a separate party outside the Congress permanently
entering councils and obstructing colonial governance from within
x: The Swarajists entered the councils to expose them as sham parliaments and obstruct their functioning from within, a strategy expressed as “End or Mend.”

s: On which date was the Swaraj Party formed?
x: Announced on 31 December 1922, it was formed on 1 January 1923 as the Congress-Khilafat Swaraj Party.

s: Which Andhra leader formed the People's Party to back the Swarajists?
x: The Pithapuram Raja formed the People's Party to back the Swarajists.

s: Who among the following was a Swarajist (pro-changer)?
x: Vithalbhai Patel was a Swarajist; the others were No-Changers.

s: What happened to the resolution relating to council entry at the Gaya Session of the Congress in December 1922?
x: C.R. Das’s resolution supporting council entry was defeated at Gaya in December 1922, leading to the subsequent formation of the Swaraj Party.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: The Swaraj Party was formed on 1 January 1923 by C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru, not in 1921.

s: When was the Swaraj Party formed?
x: The Swaraj Party of C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru was formed on 1 January 1923, not 1921.

s:
Consider the following:
1. The Swarajists favoured entry into the councils.
2. The No-Changers favoured council entry over constructive work.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: The Swarajists favoured council entry, while the No-Changers concentrated on constructive work and continued the boycott; both reunited at Belgaum in 1924.

s: Which of the following was a No-Changer after the Non-Cooperation Movement?
x: Vallabhbhai Patel was a No-Changer; Vithalbhai Patel, Motilal Nehru and C.R. Das were Swarajists.

s: What happened to C.R. Das's resolution on council entry at the Gaya session (December 1922)?
x: C.R. Das, the Gaya president, saw his council-entry resolution defeated, leading to the Swaraj Party.

s: Who among the following founded the Swaraj Party in 1923?
x: C.R. Das (president) and Motilal Nehru (secretary) formed the Swaraj Party; Jawaharlal Nehru was not a founder.

s: After the suspension of which movement was the Swaraj Party formed?
x: The Swaraj Party was formed after the Non-Cooperation Movement was suspended at Bardoli in 1922.

s: In which year was the Congress-Khilafat Swaraj Party formed?
x: It was announced on 31 December 1922 and formed on 1 January 1923.

s: Besides constructive work, what did the No-Changers favour?
x: The No-Changers focused on constructive work and continued the boycott of councils.

s: Who was the President of the Swarajist party organisation in Andhra?
x: Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao was President, Unnava Lakshminarayana Secretary and Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao Treasurer.

s: Who was the secretary of the Andhra branch of the Swaraj Party?
x: Unnava Lakshminarayana was secretary; Kaleswara Rao was president and Gadicherla treasurer.

s: Who was the treasurer of the Andhra branch of the Swaraj Party?
x: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao was the treasurer.

s: At which Congress session did the Swarajists and No-Changers reunite?
x: The two camps reunited at Belgaum (1924), the session presided over by Gandhi.

s: At which Congress session, held in Andhra in 1923, did local women serve as executive members and volunteers?
x: The 1923 Congress session was held at Kakinada in Andhra, where local women served as executive members and volunteers. Gaya (1922) was in Bihar, Belgaum (1924) in Karnataka and Nagpur (1920) in central India.

s: Why is the Belgaum session of the Indian National Congress (1924) notable?
o: It was the only Congress session presided over by Mahatma Gandhi
It adopted the Purna Swaraj resolution
It approved the suspension of the Non-Cooperation Movement
It was the first session presided over by a woman
x: Belgaum 1924 was the only INC session presided over by Gandhi, and it reunited the Swarajists and No-Changers. Purna Swaraj was adopted at Lahore (1929); the NCM was suspended at Bardoli (1922); the first woman President was Annie Besant (1917).

s: Who presided over the Kakinada session of the Congress in 1923?
x: Maulana Mohammad Ali presided over the Kakinada session (1923).

s: Who presided over the Guwahati session of the Congress in 1926?
x: S. Srinivasa Iyengar presided at Guwahati (1926).

s: Which of the following pairs of Congress session and president is correctly matched?
x: Sarojini Naidu presided at Kanpur (1925); Madras 1927 was M.A. Ansari and Gaya 1922 was C.R. Das.

s: Who presided over the Madras session of the Congress in 1927?
x: Dr. M.A. Ansari presided over the Madras session of 1927, which called for boycott of the Simon Commission.

s: What did the Delhi special session of the Indian National Congress held in September 1923 permit the Swarajists to do?
o: withdraw from the Central Legislative Assembly
x: The Delhi special session in September 1923 allowed the Swarajists to contest elections. They made substantial gains in the elections held later in 1923.

s: Which Swarajist won a Central Legislative Assembly seat from Madras in the 1923 elections?
x: In the 1923 elections V. Ramadas won a Central Legislative Assembly seat from Madras.

s: Which Congress session allowed the Swarajists to contest the 1923 elections?
x: The Delhi special session of September 1923 allowed the Swarajists to contest the elections.

s: Which bill of 1928 did the Swarajists oppose in the Central Legislative Assembly?
x: The Swarajists opposed the Public Safety Bill of 1928; earlier, their demand for review of the 1919 Act led to the Muddiman Committee.

s: Who mainly made up the Nationalist Party formed in the Central Legislative Assembly in 1924?
o: Swarajists, Jinnah’s Independents and Malaviya’s group
Congress socialists, revolutionaries and trade unions
Swarajists, British officials and Simon Commission members
x: The Nationalist Party brought together the Swarajists, Jinnah’s Independents and Malaviya’s group. It had about 70 members.

s: By what vote was Vithalbhai Patel elected President of the Central Legislative Assembly in 1925?
x: He won on 24 August 1925 by 58 to 56 against the government-backed T. Rangachariar.

s: The Muddiman Committee (1924) was the result of the Swarajist demand to review which of the following?
x: Swarajist pressure for a review of the 1919 Act led to the Muddiman Committee.

s: Who was the first elected Indian President of the Central Legislative Assembly?
x: Swarajist Vithalbhai Patel was elected in 1925, defeating T. Rangachariar by 58 to 56.

s: In which year did the Swarajists walk out of the councils after the Lahore session?
x: The Swarajists left the councils in 1930 after the Lahore session.

s: What did the Responsivists within the Swarajist movement favour?
o: the immediate abolition of the Congress
exclusive emphasis on spinning and khadi
complete withdrawal from all legislative activity
x: The Responsivists favoured cooperation with the government. Lajpat Rai, Malaviya and N.C. Kelkar were associated with this tendency.

s: When did C.R. Das die, after which the Swarajists split?
x: C.R. Das died in June 1925 and the party split.

s: Which of the following was NOT a Responsivist?
x: Lajpat Rai, Malaviya and Kelkar were Responsivists; Rajagopalachari was a No-Changer.

s: During which lull did council work and constructive work together keep the national movement alive?
x: The two camps proved complementary and kept the movement alive in the 1922-28 lull.

s: Which of the following was a part of the constructive programme of the 1920s national movement?
x: The constructive programme included khadi and spinning, removal of untouchability, Hindu-Muslim unity, prohibition, national schools and village panchayats.

s: Which of the following was NOT part of the constructive programme of the 1920s?
x: Council entry was the Swarajist strategy; untouchability removal, village panchayats and prohibition were constructive items.

s: Which of the following activities was particularly associated with women’s participation in Andhra during the constructive programme?
x: Women in Andhra participated in picketing and prohibition work as part of the constructive programme.

s: Ponduru, famed nationally for its khadi, is in which district?
x: Ponduru in Srikakulam district was famed nationally for khadi.

s: With which event did the Civil Disobedience Movement of 1930 begin?
x: The Civil Disobedience Movement began with Gandhi's Dandi March and was led by Gandhi and the INC.

s: Which of the following was central among Gandhi's demands addressed to Viceroy Irwin before the Dandi March?
o: Acceptance of the Nehru Report without change
Immediate convening of the Third Round Table Conference
x: Abolition of the salt tax was a central demand in Gandhi's eleven-point letter to Viceroy Irwin. Irwin did not accept the demands.

s:
Consider the following about the Dandi March:
1. Gandhi began it from Sabarmati Ashram on 12 March 1930 with 78 followers.
2. The route covered about 240 kilometres.
3. He broke the salt law at Dandi on 6 April 1930.
Which of the above statements are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct; statement 2 is wrong because the route was about 240 miles (385 km), not 240 km.

s: Why did Gandhi choose salt as the central symbol of the Civil Disobedience Movement?
o: It was produced exclusively in Gujarat.
It was used only by the urban middle classes.
It was a universal necessity and the salt tax visibly represented colonial exploitation.
It was connected with the demand for separate electorates.
x: Salt was consumed by both rich and poor, and the salt tax and monopoly made it a visible symbol of colonial economic exploitation.

s: What was the approximate distance covered by Gandhi in the Dandi March?
x: The march covered about 240 miles (385 km) in 24 days - not 240 km.

s: Dandi, where Gandhi broke the salt law, is in which district of Gujarat?
x: Dandi lies on the Gujarat coast in Navsari district.

s: How many days did the Dandi March from Sabarmati to Dandi take?
x: The march took 24 days; 78 is the number of followers.

s: Who compared the Dandi March to "Napoleon's return from Elba"?
x: Subhas Bose likened the Dandi March to Napoleon's march from Elba to Paris.

s: In which jail was Gandhi lodged after his arrest on 5 May 1930?
x: Gandhi was arrested on 5 May 1930 and taken to Yerwada Jail.

s: Who was named to lead the Salt Satyagraha after the arrest of Abbas Tyabji?
x: Abbas Tyabji was the first successor after Gandhi's arrest; Sarojini Naidu was the second.

s: Gandhi named which person as the first successor to lead the movement after his arrest during the Salt Satyagraha?
x: Abbas Tyabji was designated as Gandhi's first successor after his arrest. Sarojini Naidu was named the second successor.

s: Where was Gandhi arrested on the night of 4-5 May 1930?
x: Gandhi was arrested at Karadi near Dandi and taken to Yerwada Jail.

s: How many followers accompanied Gandhi on the Dandi March (12 March–6 April 1930)?
x: Gandhi marched with 78 followers, covering about 240 miles.

s: Gandhi's letter of 2 March 1930 to Lord Irwin contained how many demands?
x: The letter to Irwin carried 11 demands, the main one being abolition of the salt tax.

s: On which date did Gandhi reach Dandi?
x: He reached Dandi on 5 April and broke the salt law on 6 April 1930.

s: Who was the Viceroy when Gandhi began the Dandi March in 1930?
x: Lord Irwin was Viceroy during the Dandi March and signed the Pact of 1931; Willingdon came later.

s: Who presided over the Purna Swaraj session of the INC?
x: Jawaharlal Nehru presided over the Purna Swaraj session.

s: With what did the Calcutta session of the Congress (1928) accept the Nehru Report?
o: A one-year ultimatum to the British
A boycott of the Simon Commission only
A call for the Dandi March
x: Calcutta 1928 gave a one-year ultimatum; Purna Swaraj was adopted only at Lahore in 1929.

s: What did the Lahore Session of the Congress (December 1929) adopt?
x: With the one-year Calcutta ultimatum expired, the Lahore Session rejected Dominion Status and adopted Purna Swaraj.

s: Who was the Viceroy during the Simon Commission visit, the Lahore Purna Swaraj session and the Dandi March?
x: Lord Irwin (1926-31) was Viceroy through all three events.

s: Who was the first to pass a Purna Swaraj resolution at the district level in Andhra Pradesh?
x: Bulusu Sambamurthy of East Godavari was associated with the first district-level Purna Swaraj resolution in Andhra Pradesh.

s: Which day did the Lahore session (1929) decide to observe every year as Independence Day?
x: The Lahore session decided to observe 26 January as Independence Day; the first was on 26 January 1930.

s: Where did Jawaharlal Nehru hoist the tricolour at midnight on 31 December 1929?
o: On the banks of the Ravi
On the banks of the Sabarmati
x: After the Purna Swaraj resolution at Lahore, Nehru hoisted the tricolour on the banks of the Ravi at midnight.

s: Which of the following was NOT a resolution of the Lahore session of 1929?
o: Boycott of the Round Table Conference
Authorising the Working Committee to launch Civil Disobedience
x: Abolition of untouchability was not among the Lahore resolutions; the others were.

s: Why was 26 January chosen as the date for the Constitution of India to come into force in 1950?
o: The Congress had celebrated 26 January 1930 as the first Independence Day
The Constituent Assembly first met on that day
The Constitution was signed on that day
The Lahore session ended on that day
x: 26 January 1930 was the first Independence Day (Purna Swaraj Day), so the date was chosen for the Constitution.

s: When was the first Independence Day (Purna Swaraj Day) observed?
x: Following the Lahore resolution, the first Independence Day was observed on 26 January 1930.

s: At which place did Sarojini Naidu lead the raid in 1930?
x: Sarojini Naidu led the raid at the Dharasana Salt Works after Gandhi's arrest.

s: Which leader was associated with the Chittagong armoury raid and a proclaimed provisional government?
x: Surya Sen led the Chittagong armoury raid and proclaimed a provisional government.

s: Rani Gaidinliu, arrested in 1932, led resistance in which region?
x: Rani Gaidinliu led the movement in the Manipur/Naga hills; Nehru called her "Rani".

s: Which of the following pairs (centre - region) is correctly matched?
x: Sanikatta was the Karnataka salt satyagraha centre; Dharasana is in Gujarat and Vedaranyam in Tamil Nadu.

s: Where did protests against the Cunningham Circular take place during the CDM?
x: The Cunningham Circular protests were in Assam; the Chaukidari Tax agitation was in Bihar.

s: Who reported the beatings at the Dharasana Salt Works to the international public?
x: The beatings at Dharasana were reported by Webb Miller, a United States journalist.

s: To which place did C. Rajagopalachari lead a salt march from Trichinopoly in April 1930?
x: Rajagopalachari marched from Trichinopoly to Vedaranyam on the Tamil coast and made salt there on 30 April 1930.

s: Which future leader was imprisoned for the first time in the Vedaranyam salt march?
x: K. Kamaraj was first jailed in Rajaji's Vedaranyam salt march of 1930.

s: In which province was the Chaukidari Tax agitation carried on during the Civil Disobedience Movement?
x: The Chaukidari Tax agitation took place in Bihar, e.g. at Begusarai.

s: Where did a textile workers' rising lead to martial law in 1930, during the CDM?
x: The Sholapur textile workers' rising in 1930 led to martial law.

s: The non-violent march on the Dharasana Salt Works was led by ____ and reported to the world by ____.
x: Sarojini Naidu led the Dharasana march, where volunteers took unarmed beatings, and Webb Miller of United Press reported it. Abbas Tyabji had been arrested before it; Kamaladevi led women into the Salt Satyagraha elsewhere; Louis Fischer was not the reporter.

s: For which news agency did Webb Miller, who reported the Dharasana beatings, work?
x: Webb Miller was an American journalist of the United Press.

s: On which date did Sarojini Naidu lead the march on the Dharasana Salt Works?
x: The Dharasana march took place on 21 May 1930, with about 2,500 satyagrahis.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: K. Kelappan led the Salt March in Malabar. Gopabandhu Chaudhuri was associated with Odisha, C. Rajagopalachari with Tamil Nadu, and Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan with the NWFP.

s: Where did Satish Chandra Dasgupta lead the Salt Satyagraha in Bengal?
x: Satish Chandra Dasgupta led at Mahishbathan in 24 Parganas.

s: Who led the Salt Satyagraha in Odisha (Balasore, Cuttack, Puri)?
x: Gopabandhu Chaudhuri led the Odisha salt satyagraha.

s: Who led the Salt Satyagraha in Malabar (Kerala)?
x: K. Kelappan led in Malabar; Rajaji in Tamil Nadu.

s: K. Kamaraj was first jailed during which salt march?
x: Kamaraj was first jailed in Rajaji's Vedaranyam salt march (1930).

s: Where did the Khudai Khidmatgars mainly organise their Civil Disobedience protests?
x: The Khudai Khidmatgars, or Red Shirts, led non-violent protests in Peshawar and the North-West Frontier Province. The Qissa Khwani firing occurred there in April 1930.

s: The Garhwal Rifles became notable during the Civil Disobedience Movement because they
o: refused to fire on the crowd at Peshawar
led the salt march at Vedaranyam
x: The Garhwal Rifles, associated with Chandra Singh Garhwali, refused to fire on the crowd at Peshawar in 1930.

s: Who among the following was known as the ‘Frontier Gandhi’?
x: Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan was popularly known as the ‘Frontier Gandhi’ and was associated with the Khudai Khidmatgars.

s: Where did the Qissa Khwani firing of April 1930 take place?
x: The Qissa Khwani firing (April 1930) was in Peshawar, during the Khudai Khidmatgar protests.

s: Who led the Khudai Khidmatgar-linked Salt Satyagraha in the North-West Frontier Province?
x: Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan led the movement in the NWFP through the Khudai Khidmatgar organisation.

s: How did Babu Genu, a martyr of the Civil Disobedience Movement, die?
o: He was crushed by a lorry carrying foreign cloth in Bombay
x: Babu Genu was crushed by a lorry carrying foreign cloth in Bombay on 12 December 1930 - not at Dharasana.

s: Which of the following belongs to the Civil Disobedience Movement and NOT to the earlier revolutionary phase?
x: Babu Genu died in the CDM (1930); Khudiram, Prafulla Chaki and the Chapekars belong to 1897-1908.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
x: Babu Genu was associated with Bombay, where he was crushed by a lorry carrying foreign cloth. Dharasana was associated with Sarojini Naidu.

s: At whom was Khudiram Bose's Muzaffarpur bomb (1908) aimed?
x: Khudiram Bose targeted magistrate Kingsford in Muzaffarpur on 30 April 1908.

s: In which year did the Chapekar brothers shoot plague commissioner W.C. Rand at Pune?
x: The Chapekar brothers shot Rand in Pune in 1897 - the revolutionary phase, not the CDM.

s: Who was the first woman arrested in Nellore in connection with the national movement?
x: Paturi Balasaraswatamma was the first woman arrested in Nellore in connection with the national movement.

s: Who was the first Indian woman to preside over the Indian National Congress, and where?
x: Sarojini Naidu was the first Indian woman President of the Congress. She presided over the Kanpur session in 1925.

s:
Consider the following about women in the Civil Disobedience Movement:
1. Women joined in massive numbers, including picketing liquor and foreign-cloth shops.
2. Women participated only after the movement was withdrawn in 1934.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: The CDM was the first occasion on which women participated in massive numbers, picketing liquor shops and foreign-cloth shops.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay - led women into the Salt Satyagraha
Aruna Asaf Ali - led the Dharasana raid
Sarojini Naidu - hoisted the flag at Gowalia Tank in 1942
Kasturba Gandhi - first Indian woman President of the INC
x: Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay led women into the Salt Satyagraha. Aruna Asaf Ali hoisted the flag at Gowalia Tank in the Quit India Movement (1942); Sarojini Naidu led the Dharasana raid and was the first Indian woman INC President (Kanpur 1925); Kasturba Gandhi joined protests and was imprisoned.

s: With which of the following was the 'Kattera Udyamam' in Andhra associated?
o: the formation of the Red Shirts
increased participation of women in the Salt Satyagraha
a campaign against the Cunningham Circular
the boycott of the Round Table Conference
x: The ‘Kattera Udyamam’, or scissors movement, helped raise women’s participation in the Andhra movement.

s: To which district of Andhra did Duvvuri Subbamma, a woman leader jailed in the CDM, belong?
x: Duvvuri Subbamma was an East Godavari woman leader jailed in the CDM.

s: Aruna Asaf Ali hoisted the national flag at Gowalia Tank during which movement?
x: Aruna Asaf Ali hoisted the flag at Gowalia Tank in the Quit India Movement (1942), not the CDM.

s: Which woman leader led women into the Salt Satyagraha?
x: Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay led women into the Salt Satyagraha.

s: When did the Simon Commission arrive in India?
x: The Simon Commission was appointed in November 1927 and arrived on 3 February 1928.

s: When was the Poona Pact signed?
x: The Poona Pact was signed in September 1932; the Communal Award was announced in August 1932.

s: The First Round Table Conference (12 Nov 1930 - 19 Jan 1931) was:
x: The Congress boycotted the First RTC in London as the CDM was on.

s: On which date was the Communal Award, granting separate electorates to the depressed classes, announced?
x: The Communal Award came on 16 August 1932, before the Poona Pact of 24 September 1932.

s: On which date was the Gandhi-Irwin Pact, also called the Delhi Pact, signed?
x: The Pact was signed on 5 March 1931; dating it to March 1930 is a known trap (the Dandi March was then just beginning). 23 March 1931 is the execution of Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru; 24 September 1932 is the Poona Pact.

s: In which year was the Civil Disobedience Movement withdrawn?
x: The CDM was withdrawn in 1934, after the Gandhi-Irwin Pact (1931) and the Communal Award and Poona Pact (1932).

s: What was the main reason for the failure of the second phase of the Civil Disobedience Movement (1932–1934)?
o: Lack of any participation by peasants
Acceptance of the Communal Award by Gandhi
The absence of a Karachi Congress Session
x: The second phase of the Civil Disobedience Movement, from 1932 to 1934, failed under repression.

s:
Consider the following about the Civil Disobedience Movement:
1. It was confined exclusively to urban merchants and lawyers.
2. It was the first movement to break laws openly on a mass scale.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: The CDM was the first movement to break laws openly on a mass scale, drawing women, peasants, tribals and merchants into the struggle.

s:
Consider the following:
1. The Non-Cooperation Movement began in 1920.
2. The Quit India Movement began in 1931.
3. The Civil Disobedience Movement began in 1930.
Which of the above statements are correct?
x: Non-Cooperation began in 1920 and Civil Disobedience in 1930; statement 2 is false because Quit India began in 1942.

s: Chandra Shekhar Azad's martyrdom (27 Feb 1931) came just before which event?
x: Azad died on 27 February 1931; the Gandhi-Irwin Pact followed on 5 March 1931.

s: With which event did the first phase of the Civil Disobedience Movement end?
x: The first phase ran 1930-31 up to the Gandhi-Irwin Pact; the second phase was 1932-34.

s:
Consider the following statements about the significance of the Civil Disobedience Movement:
1. It was the first movement to break laws openly on a mass scale.
2. It brought the NWFP into the national movement.
3. Revolutionary activity merged into it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The CDM broke laws openly on a mass scale and drew in the NWFP; revolutionary activity stayed separate, so 3 is false.

s: In which year did the Cripps Mission come to India?
x: The Cripps Mission came in 1942, after Chauri Chaura (1922), the Lahore Session (1929) and the Gandhi-Irwin Pact (1931).

s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
1. Dandi March
2. Arrival of the Simon Commission
3. Purna Swaraj resolution at Lahore
4. First Round Table Conference
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Simon Commission (Feb 1928), Purna Swaraj (Dec 1929), Dandi March (March 1930), First RTC (Nov 1930).

s:
Arrange the following events in the correct chronological sequence:
I. Communal Award
II. Karachi session of the Congress
III. Cripps Mission
IV. Nehru Report
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Nehru Report (1928), Karachi session (1931), Communal Award (1932), Cripps Mission (1942).

s: Who was designated as the dictator of the Andhra Salt Satyagraha?
x: Konda Venkatappayya was the dictator of the Andhra Salt Satyagraha and had met Gandhi at Jambusar.

s: Whose idea was the district 'sibiram' (camp) with its own dictator and war council during the Salt Satyagraha in Andhra?
x: Each district had a dictator, war council and military-style camp, an idea of Pattabhi Sitaramayya.

s: What did each district have during the Civil Disobedience Movement in Andhra?
x: Every district had its own dictator, war council and camp, known as a shibiram.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: The camps included Guntur in Guntur, Pallepadu Ashram in Nellore, Bellary in Rayalaseema, and Vedavanam at Prakasam's house in Madras. Krishna was not identified with the Vedavanam camp.

s: The Pallepadu Ashram, a Civil Disobedience camp, was located in which district?
x: Pallepadu Ashram was the camp in Nellore district.

s: Where was Vedavanam, Prakasam's house that served as a CDM camp, located?
x: Vedavanam was in Madras, not in Krishna district.

s: Konda Venkatappayya was appointed 'Dictator' for Andhra during which movement?
x: The Andhra Congress Committee made Konda Venkatappayya Dictator for Andhra for the Salt Satyagraha of 1930.

s: Which of the following was part of the Civil Disobedience programme in Andhra villages?
x: The programme included making salt, picketing foreign-cloth and toddy shops, cutting toddy palms and raiding salt depots.

s: Which tax was the main target of the Civil Disobedience Movement launched in 1930?
x: The salt tax was the main target of the Civil Disobedience Movement, launched with Gandhi's Dandi March in 1930.

s: In Andhra towns, what form did the Civil Disobedience programme mainly take?
x: Towns picketed foreign-cloth shops; salt-making, cutting toddy palms and raiding salt depots were the village programme.

s: Volunteers from which institution joined the CDM in May 1930?
x: Eluru National School volunteers joined in May 1930.

s: Where did a later anti-arrack agitation by women begin in 1991?
x: Women launched the anti-arrack agitation at Dubagunta (Nellore) in 1991.

s: Who is the author of 'Andaman Jeevitam'?
x: Andaman Jeevitam was written by Prativadi Bhayankaracharyulu, who was sent to the Cellular Jail after the Kakinada bomb case.

s: Which book was written by Prativadi Bhayankaracharyulu, the accused of the Kakinada bomb case?
x: Prativadi wrote Andaman Jeevitam; Nenu Naa Desam is Darshi Chenchayya's Ghadar memoir and Bandi Jiwan is Sanyal's.

s: Which organisation was founded by Prativadi Bhayankarachari in the Godavari district around 1931?
x: Prativadi Bhayankarachari founded the Ujjeevana Bharata Samithi in the Godavari district (c. 1931) before the Kakinada bomb case.

s: In which year did the Kakinada bomb case take place?
x: The Kakinada bomb case of 1933 involved Prativadi Bhayankarachari, who got 14 years in the Cellular Jail.

s: Which CDM volunteer was lathi-charged at Rajahmundry?
x: Venneti Satyanarayana was lathi-charged at Rajahmundry; Thota Narsayya at Machilipatnam.

s: On which date did the Berhampore firing during the repression of the CDM take place?
x: The Berhampore firing was on 15 January 1932, under Lord Willingdon.

s: In which year was the Civil Disobedience Movement finally withdrawn?
x: The second phase (1932-34) ended with the CDM withdrawn in 1934.

s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
1. Gandhi-Irwin Pact
2. Gandhi's letter to Irwin with 11 demands
3. First Andhra salt satyagraha at Machilipatnam
4. Berhampore firing
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Letter to Irwin (2 March 1930), Machilipatnam (6 April 1930), Gandhi-Irwin Pact (5 March 1931), Berhampore firing (15 January 1932).

s: Which Viceroy was associated with the repression of the Civil Disobedience Movement during 1932–34?
x: Lord Willingdon was the Viceroy during the repression of the Civil Disobedience Movement in 1932–34. Lord Irwin was associated with the Gandhi-Irwin Pact.

s: Yerneni Subrahmanyam, the only Telugu marcher in the Dandi March, belonged to which district?
x: Yerneni (Erneni) Subrahmanyam of Krishna district was the only Telugu Dandi marcher; he later founded an ashram at Komaravolu.

s: Yerneni Subrahmanyam, the only Telugu Dandi marcher, later founded an ashram at which place?
x: Yerneni Subrahmanyam of Krishna district later founded an ashram at Komaravolu.

s: Who wrote the patriotic song ‘Bharata Swarajya Yuddham’?
x: Jagganna Sastri wrote ‘Bharata Swarajya Yuddham’.

s: Who is the author of the patriotic song 'Veeragandhamu Techhinaramu... Veerulevvaro Telpudee'?
x: The song was written by Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary.

s: Who led twenty women to make salt at the High Court beach in Madras?
x: Durgabai Deshmukh led twenty women in making salt at the High Court beach in Madras.

s:
Consider the following about Achanta Rukmini Lakshmipathi:
1. She was the first woman graduate in Andhra and the first woman arrested in the Salt Satyagraha.
2. She led twenty women to make salt at the High Court beach in Madras.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: Achanta Rukmini Lakshmipathi was the first woman graduate in Andhra and the first woman arrested in the Salt Satyagraha; the High Court beach march of twenty women was led by Durgabai Deshmukh.

s: Which of the following describes women's role in the Andhra Civil Disobedience Movement?
o: They took part only in symbolic gatherings
They joined in large numbers, making salt, picketing and courting imprisonment
Their role was confined to national leaders outside Andhra
x: The Civil Disobedience Movement brought women into the Andhra struggle in large numbers, including salt-making, picketing and imprisonment.

s: Where was Achanta Rukmini Lakshmipathi arrested in the Salt Satyagraha?
x: She was arrested at Vedaranyam after Rajaji's arrest, on 15 May 1930.

s: Who carried the 'Swarajya Lakshmi Vratam' door to door on Ugadi in Guntur?
x: Unnava Lakshmibayamma ran the Swarajya Lakshmi Vratam on Ugadi in Guntur.

s: Who was identified as the only Telugu marcher in the Dandi March?
x: Yerneni Subramanyam was identified as the only Telugu marcher in the Dandi March.

s: Who was the first woman arrested in the Salt Satyagraha in Andhra?
